Here's a passage about Directed Acyclic Graphs using all standard punctuation marks:

A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) has a simple rule: no cycles allowed! While regular graphs can loop back on themselves, DAGs must flow in one direction; this makes them perfect for modeling dependencies. Consider these examples: task scheduling, version control systems, and genealogical trees. "But what if I need to represent circular relationships?!" you might ask‽ Well, that's when you'll need a different data structure: perhaps a cyclic graph would be better. DAGs have many applications — from build systems to workflow management — and their popularity stems from their clarity... After all, who doesn't love a straightforward, loop-free structure?
